title: Six Calls for Arbitrary-Arity Correlation Intractability
summary: Correlation intractability is fully covered only for constant-arity evasive relations; whether six random-function calls are necessary at arbitrary arity remains open.

formal_statement.body: For correlation intractability with evasive relations of arity $k$, the available result fully covers only constant arity $k=O(1)$. Its proof fails for larger $k$, although no counterexamples showing attacks are known. Determine whether six calls to a random function are necessary for correlation intractability at arbitrary arity.

scope.domain: Correlation intractability for evasive relations and random-function-based cryptographic constructions.
parameters: k: arity of the evasive relation
Number of random-function calls: resource count whose necessity is assessed, with six as the candidate value
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether six calls to a random function are necessary for correlation intractability at arbitrary arity.

citations.label: Naor-Reingold Goes Public: The Complexity of Known-Key Security

progress.summary: The source presents this as a limitation: full coverage holds for constant arity, while the proof inherently fails for larger arities and no attacks are known. It leaves the necessity of six random-function calls at arbitrary arity for future work.
